See also: Amarillo

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish amariello, from Late Latin amarellus, from Latin amarus (“bitter, sour”), probably connected to the yellowish colour of bile; or from Arabic عَنْبَر (ʕanbar, “ambergris”), from Middle Persian 𐭠𐭭𐭡𐭫 (ʾnbl /⁠ambar⁠/, “ambergris”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /amaˈɾiʝo/ [a.maˈɾi.ʝo]
  • IPA(key): /amaˈɾiʝo/ [a.maˈɾi.ʝo] (Equatorial Guinea, most of Latin America and Spain)
  • IPA(key): /amaˈɾiʎo/ [a.maˈɾi.ʎo] (Andes Mountains, rustic northern Spain, Paraguay, Philippines)
  • IPA(key): /amaˈɾiʃo/ [a.maˈɾi.ʃo] (Buenos Aires and environs)
  • IPA(key): /amaˈɾiʒo/ [a.maˈɾi.ʒo] (elsewhere in Argentina and Uruguay)

  • Audio (Spain):(file)
 
  • Rhymes: -iʝo
  • Rhymes: -iʝo (Equatorial Guinea, most of Latin America and Spain)
  • Rhymes: -iʎo (Andes Mountains, rustic northern Spain, Paraguay, Philippines)
  • Rhymes: -iʃo (Buenos Aires and environs)
  • Rhymes: -iʒo (elsewhere in Argentina and Uruguay)

  • Syllabification: a‧ma‧ri‧llo

Adjective

[edit]

amarillo (feminine amarilla, masculine plural amarillos, feminine plural amarillas)

  1. yellow or golden (colour)
  2. (heraldry) or (colour on a coat of arms)
    Synonym: oro

Noun

[edit]

amarillo m (plural amarillos)

  1. yellow
  2. (colloquial) whitey (British: sickness, especially when induced by cannabis use)

Related terms

[edit]
  • amargo

Verb

[edit]

amarillo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of amarillar

[edit]

  • English: Amarillo
  • → Tagalog: amarilyo
